To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
39 % of ESSR scientific abstracts were already PubMed cited within 2 year of the congress.
39 % of ESSR scientific abstracts were in print within 3 years after submission to the congress and that 6 % were already PubMed cited before the congress.
45 % of ESSR scientific abstracts are published in print and 39 % are published within 2 years of the congress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the time from idea to publication.
the time interval from abstract submission to publication of scientific research results.
the publication rate of scientific abstract at the 2008 and the 2009 European Society of Skeletal Radiology (ESSR) congresses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
45 % of the ESSR scientific abstracts were cited within 2 % years.
the duration of intellectual properties of ESSR abstracts is 2 years in 39 % of the cases.
45 % of ESSR scientific abstracts were already published in print until September of 2012 and 39 % within 2 year after the congress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a research proposal should have a duration of 2 to 5 years from idea until publication.
39 % of all abstracts presented at the ESSR congress were published in a journal within 2 year of the congress.
a research proposal can be published in 2 years.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the duration of intellectual ownership is shorter than previously assumed.
the 2-year duration of intellectual property from idea to publication is not realistic.
a large proportion of ESSR scientific abstracts are published within 2 years of the congress.
